summary: Backend regression verified for AWS S3 proxy-serving + auto-repair. 9/10 pytest cases pass. s3-test returns exactly the 4 expected steps (Connect to bucket / Upload test file / Read file back / Cleanup test file), public=true, repaired_refs is a valid int, and completes in <2s end-to-end via public ingress. Branding logos (logo_light/logo_dark) are rewritten to /api/media/s3/... proxy URLs and no longer contain s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com. The proxy endpoint GET /api/media/s3/{key} serves 200 with image content-type for an existing branding SVG (image/svg+xml) and correctly returns 404 for a non-existent key. Auth guards on s3-test / s3-migrate return 401 without token. Invalid-cred override returns ok=false with a friendly error and a failed 'Connect to bucket' step. Media upload regression passes (POST /api/media/upload returns a url). One real backend bug found: POST /api/admin/integrations/s3-migrate is broken.

critical.issue: Endpoint 500s / 502 timeouts. Backend traceback: FileNotFoundError: '/app/backend/uploads/brand/d2fe266c7238410f926b8d6580dec63f.webp' at storage_service.py:320 (_sync_migrate calls p.read_bytes() without existence check). The DB has media refs whose local files were already deleted from prior migrations; the migrator crashes on the first missing file instead of skipping/removing the stale ref. First public call took >60s and got Cloudflare 502; second call surfaced the 500. This means the required test 'must NOT return needs_public anymore and returns ok=true with migrated/total/updated_refs/removed_local' cannot be satisfied end-to-end today.

action_items: Fix storage_service._sync_migrate: wrap `p.read_bytes()` in try/except FileNotFoundError; on missing local, either skip the ref or delete the stale local reference and continue (increment removed_local). Also consider a per-file try/except so a single bad row cannot fail the whole migration.

Consider chunking / async offloading of s3-migrate or returning immediately with a job id, because a large migration can exceed the Cloudflare 60s ingress timeout even when the work itself would succeed.
After the fix, re-run /app/backend/tests/test_s3_proxy_integration.py::test_s3_migrate_admin to confirm ok=true and absence of needs_public.
critical_code_review_comments: storage_service._sync_migrate reads every local file with p.read_bytes() without existence guard — any stale DB ref crashes the entire migration (see traceback in backend.err.log).
s3-migrate is a synchronous long-running loop wrapped in anyio.to_thread; behind Cloudflare (60s hard limit) it will 502 for any real-world bucket. Should be job/queue-based or paginated.
The controller returns the migrate result as-is with no HTTPException catch — a mid-loop crash yields a plain 500 with no context to the caller.

success_rate.frontend: not-fully-tested (login worked via one-click admin, but automated navigation to admin integrations UI could not be validated in this run; prior iteration + human screenshots confirmed the redesigned panel)

context_for_next_testing_agent: The s3 proxy-serving flow (test-connection with 4 steps, public=true, repaired_refs, branding URL rewrite, GET /api/media/s3/{key} proxy fetch, 404 on missing key, invalid override handling, auth guards, media upload regression) is fully green. The only outstanding issue is s3-migrate crashing on missing local files (FileNotFoundError in _sync_migrate). Once E1 fixes that, re-run test_s3_migrate_admin in /app/backend/tests/test_s3_proxy_integration.py. Prior human-verified screenshots already confirmed the redesigned Test panel + green health badge + logo rendering on Branding page.
rca of the issue: s3-migrate: storage_service._sync_migrate iterates every media DB row and calls Path(local_path).read_bytes() unconditionally. When a prior run already migrated & unlinked the local file but the DB row was not fully cleaned, or when files were manually removed, the very first missing path raises FileNotFoundError, aborting the whole loop. Reproduction: POST /api/admin/integrations/s3-migrate as admin -> either 502 (loop still running past 60s) or 500 with the traceback shown above. Mitigation: replace `data = p.read_bytes()` with `try: data = p.read_bytes() except FileNotFoundError: # mark row as needing url refresh / drop stale ref / continue`. Additionally guard the outer for-loop with per-item try/except so a single corrupt row cannot poison the batch, and increment removed_local for rows whose local file no longer exists.
